newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada accuses Clyde of empty promises.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada accuses Clyde of empty promises.

text.p: Gulf Canada lashed out at its bid target Clyde Petroleum on Tuesday, saying the company had poor development prospects and accusing Clyde's management of making empty promises.
"Clyde shareholders have a choice: the certainty of 105 pence in cash today against the empty promises of Clyde's directors," said J.P Bryan, president and chief executive of Gulf Canada.
Clyde earlier said Gulf's offer severely undervalued the British oil exploration and production sector. Gulf Canada reacted by saying Clyde used unaccepted methods.
"Clyde's board has abandoned accepted valuation methods and moved the discussion on value into the realm of fantasy," said Bryan.
Bryan said Clyde had a mature asset portfolio with declining reserves and reserve life with limited development opportunities and exploration prospects.
"Clyde's strategy...is highly unlikely to deliver any real growth in value to shareholders," he said.
Gulf Canada launched its 432 million stg bid from Clyde in December. Clyde's shares were down 2-1/2 pence to 120-1/2 pence by 1257 GMT.
